- How to test (2 machines / 2 instances, manual GUI equivalent): Machine/Window A: MainMenu -> Host (port 7777). Machine/Window B: MainMenu -> Join 127.0.0.1:7777 (or A's LAN IP). Not wired into CI (see report recommendation to producer/tools-devops). Logs are written to the OS temp dir, gitignored, never into the repo tree.

design_ruling: DESIGN RULING (human/producer, 2026-07-15, recorded Change Log [0.42]) -- observed during TK-P2-09's human pass that a Tiger can currently walk out of the Safe Circle; this is NOT a bug, it is exactly this card's scope (boundary logic doesn't exist yet). Implement per this ruling: (1) Tiger is CONFINED inside the circle -- an invisible wall at radius 5.0m (locked value, Game_Balance.md / Change Log [0.34]) blocks the Tiger from exiting; (2) Outer/human players may freely enter AND exit the circle (must be able to walk in to Kick the Tiger and flee back out); (3) host-authoritative -- the HOST clamps/rejects position, a client cannot walk a Tiger through the boundary by local movement alone (same server-authority invariant as TK-P1/TK-P2's other movement+role systems). If any part of this is ambiguous when implementation starts, escalate to `designer` before deviating (per CLAUDE.md change-control), do not guess.
notes: HUMAN 2-INSTANCE CHECKLIST (qa-engineer, 2026-07-16 -- ready to run; same style/temp-debug approach as TK-P2-02/03/09's own human passes: add scoped TEMPORARY debug prints, run, then REVERT them + re-confirm GUT 276/276). This card touches host-authoritative Tiger position + a live correction @rpc, so a human pass is REQUIRED before Done (see QA VERDICT in review_verdicts). Open 2+ instances (ideally also N=3-4 once for the multi-Outer case) through the real WaitingRoom -> Start Match flow; a live Tiger must exist -- first-Tiger assignment (TK-P2-09) is now DONE, so a real Tiger is produced by the ordinary flow (no F7 hook needed). PREP -- temporarily print, HOST-SIDE, inside GameManager.correct_tiger_position() AND _apply_tiger_position_correction() (and/or a per-tick line in the host _physics_process() loop's correction branch): whenever a correction is actually issued, print the target peer_id + the pre/post position + horizontal distance; ALSO on every peer print each Tiger Player's replicated position each ~0.5s. Leave the host's existing logs on. CASE 1 (Tiger CONFINED -- design ruling pt 1, the core AC): on the machine OWNING the Tiger, walk the Tiger straight at the Safe Circle edge and hold W into the wall, then walk along/around the full perimeter. The Tiger must visibly STOP at the ring (radius 5.0m) and be unable to walk out in any direction; walking at an angle should slide along the wall, not pass through. Confirm the invisible wall behaves as infinite height -- jump (Space) while pressed against the wall must NOT let the Tiger clear it. FAIL if the Tiger's own client ever renders its body outside the ring under ordinary movement. CASE 2 (Tiger confinement AGREES across windows -- design ruling pt 3): on EVERY OTHER window's replicated copy of that same Tiger, confirm it also stays at/inside the ring (never seen outside on any screen) while the owner pushes the wall. FAIL (S1 desync) if any window shows the Tiger inside while another shows it outside, or the Tiger's position visibly disagrees between windows by more than normal interp lag. CASE 3 (correction path is a TOTAL NO-OP in honest steady state -- THE EXACT BUG JUST FIXED, highest-priority check): with an honest Tiger sitting PINNED against the wall (hold W into the boundary for 10+ seconds, the single most common resting state this feature creates), watch the HOST's temp correction log. There must be ZERO (or at most a rare, isolated, non-repeating) correction line -- NOT a steady 15-30/sec stream. Simultaneously there must be NO visible rubber-banding / stutter / position snap-back on the Tiger on ANY window while it rests at the wall. FAIL if the host spams correction RPCs against the wall-pinned honest Tiger, or if any window shows the Tiger jittering/rubber-banding at the wall -- that is the network-engineer-found defect regressing. CASE 4 (Outer moves FREELY in/out -- design ruling pt 2): as an Outer/human player, walk INTO the Safe Circle (to reach kicking range of the Tiger) and back OUT again, repeatedly, from several directions. The Outer must cross the boundary FREELY both ways with no clamp, no stop, no correction. Confirm on both the Outer's own window and a remote window. FAIL if an Outer is ever blocked at, or snapped back from, the ring. CASE 5 (role swap keeps the boundary correct -- if a tag can be triggered live): trigger a Tag Sequence so the Tiger and an Outer swap roles; confirm the NEW Tiger immediately becomes confined (Case 1 behavior) and the freshly-demoted ex-Tiger (now Outer) can immediately walk out freely (Case 4 behavior). FAIL if confinement sticks to the wrong player or fails to transfer. VERDICT RULE: any Tiger that walks out of the circle on any window, any cross-window disagreement on Tiger position (S1), any correction-RPC spam or visible rubber-banding against an honest wall-pinned Tiger (the fixed bug regressing), any Outer blocked at the boundary, or any crash = FAIL -> back to gameplay-engineer (file bug w/ severity + RTM link). All Cases 1-4 green (Case 5 is bonus if a live tag is convenient) = recommend producer close TK-P2-06 as done. REMEMBER to REVERT the temp debug prints and re-run GUT (must stay 276/276) before closing.

review_verdicts: CODE-REVIEW VERDICT (2026-07-15): APPROVE-WITH-NITS -> qa-engineer. Pure math (radial clamp, horizontal-only/Y-preserved), role gate (Tiger-only, Outer+unrecognized both pass through unchanged), TK-P1-06 non-authority-no-op invariant, and radius consistency (5.0 in both exports + Game_Balance.md, no drift) all verified correct with dedicated test coverage. 2 non-blocking flags: (1) architect/designer -- correct_tiger_position only ever writes the OWNING peer (position is owner-authoritative one-way sync per Game_Balance.md §1), so against a genuinely malicious client that skips its own clamp, the correction is overwritten by that same client's very next authoritative tick -- a truly malicious Tiger still RENDERS outside the circle on every screen; the RPC only helps a cooperating/transient-bug client, which is narrower than ruling point 3's literal wording. This mirrors the already-approved apply_role_switch pattern and is a defense-in-depth-vs-true-containment question, not a defect -- architect/designer should rule whether Phase 2 accepts this level or a follow-up (host-authoritative Tiger position) is warranted. (2) same boundary-jitter RPC concern as network-engineer's finding below (routed there as the domain owner). Minor nits (non-blocking): host loop reads local .position not .global_position (fine while Players root = world origin, add a note/assert if that ever changes); host-side half not GUT-covered (matches existing TagSequence host-only convention, manual-pipeline only). NETWORK-ENGINEER VERDICT (2026-07-15): NOT network-safe as-is -- 1 REQUIRED fix before trusting past automation (blocks qa/human pass): SafeCircleRules.is_inside()'s exact `<=` check (no epsilon) means the host reads the owner's own float32-clamped-to-exactly-radius position and roughly half the time sees it as a few ULP OUTSIDE due to replication round-trip -- since 'Tiger pinned against the wall' is the single most common gameplay state this boundary creates, this fires a broadcast-to-ALL-peers reliable correction RPC ~15-30x/sec/Tiger against an HONEST, already-compliant client (not a rare edge case). Fix: host check must use `is_inside(pos, radius + EPSILON)` (real slack, e.g. 0.05-0.1m, not a few float ULP). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED alongside: (a) target correct_tiger_position to the owning peer only via rpc_id() instead of an all-peers broadcast (only the owner ever acts on it); (b) correct the GameManager.gd:508 comment ('This is that stop') -- confirms code-reviewer's Flag 1 independently: position is owner-authoritative so a determined cheater oscillates rather than being contained; do not describe this as an authoritative stop, and if literal containment is required that is an architecture change for `architect`, out of this card's scope. Authority correctness (host-only-sendable, cannot be spoofed to move another peer's Tiger), scope discipline (networking/NetworkManager.gd untouched), and cost/frequency at normal (non-jitter) rates all PASS. BOTH REVIEWS CONVERGE on the same concrete defect (exact-boundary check -> spurious RPC spam) -- REQUIRED fix before advancing to qa-engineer. CASE 2 (round TIMES OUT and every window agrees on the SAME new Tiger -- the core AC + the S1 check): with the shortened duration, let a round run to timeout WITHOUT anyone landing a successful Tag (just wait it out). FAIL (S1 desync) if any two windows name different new Tigers, or if a window still shows the OLD Tiger while another shows the new one beyond normal interp lag. OPTIONAL temp debug -- the ability already logs on the owning peer `[POUNCE] burst fired (owner=<name>) -- awaiting host confirm` on activation and `[POUNCE] rejected: <reason> -- burst cancelled` on a host rejection, and the HOST logs `[POUNCE] tiger <id> burst` on a validated fire + every peer logs `[POUNCE] confirmed: tiger=<id>`; watch the consoles to cross-check what you see on screen. For a precise position read, temporarily print each Tiger Player's replicated position each ~0.5s on every peer (REVERT after).  CASE 1 (owner-side burst in the held WASD direction, feels INSTANT -- core feel AC): on the window OWNING the Tiger, hold a movement key (e.g. W) and press RIGHT MOUSE BUTTON. The Tiger must immediately lurch in the held direction with NO perceptible windup/charge delay (the burst executes owner-side on the same input, not after a host round-trip), cover roughly ~2.8m (8.0 m/s x 0.35s), then smoothly return to normal WASD walking speed under your control. Try each of W/A/S/D and a diagonal -- the burst goes in the currently-held direction each time. FAIL if there is a visible charge-up delay before the dash, if the dash direction ignores the held key, or if control does not return to normal WASD after the burst ends.  CASE 2 (no-key FALLBACK to camera-forward -- documented behavior): on the Tiger's window, with NO movement key held, aim the camera somewhere and press RIGHT MOUSE BUTTON. The Tiger must burst straight along its current camera-forward direction (not a degenerate zero-length no-op). Rotate the camera and repeat -- the burst follows where the camera looks. FAIL if pressing pounce with no WASD produces no movement at all, or bursts in a direction unrelated to the camera facing.  CASE 3 (REPLICATION -- THE CORE AC, the one thing no automated probe can observe): while the Tiger pounces (CASE 1/2), watch EVERY OTHER window's replicated copy of that Tiger. Each remote window must show the SAME burst movement -- the Tiger visibly lurches the same ~2.8m in the same direction at roughly the same time -- carried by ordinary owner-authoritative position sync (the same path plain WASD/jump already replicate through, no ability-layer replication involved). FAIL (treat as the S1-class defect for this card) if any remote window does NOT show the burst, shows the Tiger rubber-banding / snapping back after the dash, or ends the burst at a visibly different spot than where the owner's own window put the Tiger (beyond normal interpolation lag).  CASE 4 (cannot pounce THROUGH the 5.0m Safe Circle wall): stand the Tiger just INSIDE the Safe Circle boundary facing OUT, hold the outward direction, and pounce toward/through the ring. The Tiger must STILL stop at the 5.0m wall -- apply_safe_circle_boundary() runs as a post-move clamp on top of the burst velocity, so a burst cannot punch the Tiger outside (burst reach ~2.8m is under the 5.0m radius by design anyway, but this explicitly proves the clamp wins over the burst). Confirm on BOTH the Tiger's own window and a remote window. FAIL if a pounce ever renders the Tiger's body outside the ring on ANY window.  CASE 5 (COOLDOWN enforcement, ~2.0s): spam RIGHT MOUSE BUTTON repeatedly. Only the FIRST press within each ~2.0s window should produce a burst; further presses inside that window must do nothing (the host rejects them). The HOST console should log `[POUNCE] tiger <id> burst` only once per ~2s despite the spam, and the owning peer should log `[POUNCE] rejected: cooldown -- burst cancelled` for the rejected presses. BEST-EFFORT / OPTIONAL sub-check (do NOT fail the card on an ambiguous read): confirm a rejected press does NOT produce a phantom/partial burst on the Tiger's own screen -- because owner-side prediction fires the burst on press and on_rejected() -> cancel_pounce_burst() stops it, a rejected press that raced the prediction should cancel within a physics tick with no meaningful movement (a very brief tick-scale twitch on a raced press is acceptable, not a bug). If the cooldown timing is hard to eyeball precisely, record the observation and move on -- an ambiguous read here is NOT a FAIL.  CASE 6 (OPTIONAL / best-effort -- pounce during a Tag Sequence is rejected by the sequence_active guard): if you can time it, press RIGHT MOUSE BUTTON during the ~1.2-1.5s Tag Sequence window right after a successful Tag (the grab/throw/transform animation, while the sequence is mid-play). host_validate()'s sequence_active guard should reject it -- the HOST should NOT log a `[POUNCE] tiger <id> burst` for that press, and the owning peer logs `[POUNCE] rejected: sequence_active -- burst cancelled`. This is HARD to time by hand in a live 2-instance session (the window is short and the pouncing player may be the one being transformed) -- consistent with how TK-P2-07's own CASE 5 handled a similarly-hard-to-isolate check: if this is not cleanly testable this session, record it as DEFERRED/UNCOVERED rather than failing the card. The guard's logic is already covered pure-side by test_pounce_rules.gd's on_rejected(sequence_active) case.  VERDICT RULE: any remote window failing to show the burst / showing rubber-banding / a cross-window end-position disagreement (CASE 3, the S1-class check for this card), a Tiger bursting OUTSIDE the 5.0m ring on any window (CASE 4), a visible charge-up delay or wrong-direction burst (CASE 1/2), Pounce ever triggering a Tag/catch (scope violation), or any crash = FAIL -> back to gameplay-engineer (file a bug w/ severity + RTM link, move the card to Doing). CASES 1-4 all green (CASE 5's cooldown no-phantom sub-check + CASE 6 mid-sequence are optional/deferrable, their ambiguity is an accepted limitation not a blocker) = recommend producer close TK-P2-18 as done. REMEMBER to REVERT any temp debug prints and re-run GUT (must stay 309/309) before closing.

title: Test-isolation: NetworkManager host()/disconnect_from_game() poisons the shared SceneTree MultiplayerAPI for alphabetically-later GUT scripts (is_server()/get_unique_id() break for any later Player.tscn authority test)
note: Discovered + reproduced (standalone repro script) while writing tests/test_role_state_machine.gd (TK-P2-04). GUT runs every tests/*.gd script in ONE shared process/SceneTree. tests/test_network_manager.gd's host()/join() tests assign a REAL ENetMultiplayerPeer to get_tree().get_multiplayer() -- the SAME root MultiplayerAPI every node in every OTHER test script also uses -- then clear it back to null on teardown. Empirically, Godot's SceneMultiplayer treats 'never had a peer' (is_server() conveniently defaults true, offline-friendly single-player default) and 'had a real peer, now cleared' (is_server() now correctly reports FALSE, get_unique_id() errors -- a real disconnected client should NOT still claim to be the server) as two DIFFERENT internal states, not the same 'offline' state. Once ANY test script assigns a real peer even once, EVERY test script that runs LATER in the same process and touches Player.tscn's is_multiplayer_authority()/get_unique_id() (CameraComponent._ready(), AbilityController._enter_tree(), etc.) inherits the 'disconnected' (not 'offline') state and fails with engine errors GUT treats as test failures. This is invisible in production (a real process only ever hosts/joins/stays offline once for its whole lifetime) and was invisible in this suite only because tests/test_ability_system.gd (the only pre-existing Player.tscn-instantiating test) happens to sort alphabetically BEFORE test_network_manager.gd -- not because it was actually safe; test_role_state_machine.gd sorts AFTER it and was the first to surface this. Worked around LOCALLY in test_role_state_machine.gd's own before_all() (resets the SceneTree's MultiplayerAPI to a fresh MultiplayerAPI.create_default_interface() instance) -- deliberately test-file-scoped, does NOT touch networking/NetworkManager.gd or any production/authority code (outside gameplay-engineer's authority per CLAUDE.md). Proper suite-wide fix belongs to whoever owns test infra/NetworkManager (tools-devops/network-engineer): either give test_network_manager.gd's peer-touching tests their OWN isolated MultiplayerAPI/root path (SceneTree.set_multiplayer(api, path)) instead of hijacking the shared root one, or add a GUT-level teardown hook that resets the root MultiplayerAPI after any test that assigns a real peer, so future test files don't depend on alphabetical-ordering luck the way test_ability_system.gd/test_role_state_machine.gd currently do.

title: [S2] Start-Match readiness-barrier grace-timer (8s) force-disconnects a legit unfocused client -- recurring, blocks team 2-instance testing
human_pass_result: PASS (2026-07-19, human 2-instance). Client alt-tabbed/backgrounded during Start Match was NOT force-disconnected; both windows landed in the arena with both Players present, no origin-stack/desync. Producer closes TK-P2-30.
labels: bug, phase-2, prio-high, S2, network, followup
fix_note: network-engineer, 2026-07-18. ROOT CAUSE (identified + documented, not guessed): an occluded/backgrounded OS window's frame loop is throttled hard by the OS compositor + vsync (down to a handful of fps while occluded). Godot drives BOTH scene-load completion (deferred change_scene_to_file -> TestArena instancing -> PlayerSpawner._ready()) AND the multiplayer poll/flush that actually SENDS the queued reliable _rpc_arena_ready packet from that same main loop -- so a healthy-but-backgrounded client's readiness legitimately lands well past the 8s ARENA_READY_GRACE_SEC, and the old grace timer force-disconnected it as if crashed. Confirmed this is stock engine+OS behavior, NOT a project misconfig: project.godot sets no low_processor_usage_mode / max_fps / vsync override (all Godot defaults). FIX (server-side, host stays fully authoritative -- evaluated all 3 human-suggested directions): chose (b) + a defensible reframing of (a); REJECTED (a)-alone (a blind bigger timeout is indefensible -- an occluded window can throttle arbitrarily long, no fixed number is safe) and did NOT apply (c) here (forcing a backgrounded window to keep rendering/flushing is a rendering/perf-domain change with side effects, and the broader 'backgrounded client in a LIVE match also stops replicating' problem is bigger than this barrier -- flagged for TK-P2-20 / architect, see below). title: Architect ruling: does Safe Circle's host-authoritative containment (TK-P2-06 point 3) need true host-authoritative Tiger position, or is owner-authoritative + best-effort host correction acceptable for Phase 2?
note: Filed from TK-P2-06's parallel code-reviewer + network-engineer reviews (2026-07-15), both independently flagging the same gap. The design ruling for TK-P2-06 (Change Log [0.42]) says 'host clamps/rejects position, a client cannot walk a Tiger through the boundary by local movement alone.' The implementation's host-side backstop (managers/GameManager.gd correct_tiger_position RPC) only writes to the OWNING peer, because Tiger position is owner-authoritative one-way sync (Game_Balance.md §1, same model as every other Player position). A genuinely malicious client that skips its own local clamp will have its very next authoritative physics tick overwrite the host's correction and re-replicate the out-of-bounds position -- so a determined cheater's Tiger still renders OUTSIDE the circle on every screen; the RPC only helps a cooperating/transient-bug client. This mirrors the already-approved apply_role_switch pattern and is not a defect in TK-P2-06's implementation -- it's a faithful application of the existing owner-authoritative position architecture. QUESTION FOR ARCHITECT: is this defense-in-depth level acceptable for Phase 2 (prove-the-loop, not yet anti-cheat-hardened), or does ruling point 3 require a follow-up card for true host-authoritative Tiger position (an architecture change -- host owns position for the Tiger role specifically, or more broadly)? NON-BLOCKING -- does not block TK-P2-06 advancing through qa/human-pass; the honest-client path (the only path physically reachable in the current human-testing process) is unaffected either way. If architect rules 'acceptable as-is', close this card with that ruling recorded in Change Log; if a host-authoritative-position change is warranted, this card becomes the spec for a new implementation card.

title: Kick targeting bug: KickAbility.host_validate() still targets nearest-any-player, never filtered to role == tiger
note: Filed from TK-P2-17 (Kick Stagger) code review (2026-07-16/17), found by the TK-P2-17 implementer and independently confirmed by code-reviewer. characters/abilities/KickAbility.gd host_validate() builds its candidate list from EVERY other CharacterBody3D under the Players root with NO role == RoleRules.TIGER filter, then hands off to the (deliberately role-agnostic) KickRules.nearest_target(). SEVERITY: real gameplay-correctness bug for N>=3, not S0/S1 -- not a crash, not a desync (host-authoritative, deterministic), but in any 3+ player session an Outer players Kick can land on and be CONFIRMED against another Outer instead of the Tiger. title: [S2] Kick Stagger never applies -- on_confirmed() gate checks the KICKER's own node instead of resolving the TARGET, permanently-false condition = dead code
note: Filed from TK-P2-17's human 2-instance test (2026-07-18): 12 kicks landed on the Tiger, zero stagger observed, zero [KICK] stagger applied locally log line. Root cause confirmed from code by the human tester: characters/abilities/KickAbility.gd's on_confirmed() runs, via the rpc_confirm call_local broadcast, on the KICKER's own ability instance on every peer (Kick is owned by the acting Outer's AbilityController). Inside it, _body is therefore always the KICKER's own Player node -- never the target's. The stagger gate checks _body.role == RoleRules.TIGER (the kicker is by definition never Tiger) AND String(_body.name) == String(target_id) (the kicker's own name is by definition never the target id) -- both permanently false for the node this code actually runs on. MovementComponent.start_stagger() is structurally unreachable through this path at any N. Full repro + fix direction is recorded in TK-P2-17's human_test_result field -- read that first. FIX: inside on_confirmed(), resolve the TARGET Player node (e.g. players_root.get_node(target_id)), gate on target_node.is_multiplayer_authority() (am I the client that owns the targeted player) instead of identity-matching _body, then call stagger on the resolved target's MovementComponent -- matching the design's own stated intent that stagger is owner-side local physics on the TARGET, not the kicker. Preserve the existing degenerate kicker-not-found -> ZERO-direction fallback semantics (just re-anchor it to compute direction from the resolved target's position, not _body's). Regression: same class as TK-P2-32 (wiring/glue dead-code invisible to pure-function GUT) -- add a scene-tree-level test that simulates a confirmed kick on a real Tiger node owned by the local peer and asserts is_staggered flips true / the stagger log fires, not just that host_validate()/on_confirmed() run without crashing. Do not close without a human 2-instance re-run of TK-P2-17's CASE 1 + CASE 2 (this is the exact surface that just failed) -- do NOT flip TK-P2-17 back to review-pending-human until this bug is fixed, reviewed, and QA'd.
fix_result: FIXED (gameplay-engineer, 2026-07-18). note: Filed from the human's CASE E bot-harness run (2026-07-26, same session as TK-BUG-P3-01 -- see that card for the log source). ROOT CAUSE (read managers/GameManager.gd ~L642-663 and ~L709-734): _on_any_player_role_changed_for_match_end() DOES correctly guard 'if match_state != PLAYING: return' before incrementing the round counter (so it does NOT double-trigger _end_match() or miscount -- that part is correct), but start_tag_sequence() (~L714, the actual entry point TagAbility.host_apply() calls once a Tag is host_validate()'d) only checks TagSequenceRules.can_start_sequence(_is_tag_sequence_active) (the re-trigger lock) -- it never checks match_state at all. The FIRST sequence's own step7 clears _is_tag_sequence_active right as/after MATCH_END fires, so nothing stops a SECOND Tag request (the bot immediately retries every tick) from validating and running a full 7-step sequence + role swap + round restart during MATCH_END. RoundManager.gd (_on_any_player_role_changed(), ~L174-180, and _on_round_timeout()) is similarly unaware of match_state entirely by design (see that file's own class doc -- deliberately decoupled from GameManager) so it restarts its round timer on ANY role_changed into Tiger regardless of match phase. FIX DIRECTION: gate start_tag_sequence() (and, per the human's ask, ideally KickAbility's stagger-applying path too for consistency/future-proofing, though it was not observed racing in this trace) on GameManager.match_state == PLAYING -- add a read-only accessor (e.g. is_match_playing(), mirroring the existing is_sequence_active() accessor TagAbility.host_validate() already calls at ~L148) and check it in TagAbility.host_validate() (reject the Tag validation itself, the earliest choke point) AND/OR in start_tag_sequence() as defense-in-depth (mirroring the existing 'defense in depth, should be unreachable in practice' comment already on the can_start_sequence() check). title: [Check/off-by-one] match-end trigger fires at the START of round rounds_per_match, not its end -- a 3-round match only actually plays 2 full rounds

note: Filed from the human's CASE E bot-harness run (2026-07-26, same session as TK-BUG-P3-01/02) as an explicit 'please check' item -- this is NOT a newly-discovered defect, it is the SAME off-by-one code-reviewer already flagged as non-blocking NIT N1 on TK-P2-15's own code_review field ('rounds_per_match currently means Tiger-assignments-before-end, i.e. N-1 played rounds'), now confirmed live: host log shows round 1 (tiger=912678832, 05:55:58) and round 2 (tiger=1117663808, 05:56:01) both play out with a real Tag exchange, but the moment round 3/3 is announced ('[MATCH] round 3/3 started', 05:56:04) the VERY SAME log line is immediately followed by '[MATCH] match-end trigger reached (3/3 rounds) -- ending match' at the identical timestamp -- round 3 gets zero play time before the match ends. Root cause confirmed in managers/GameManager.gd's _on_any_player_role_changed_for_match_end() (~L653-661): _round_count is incremented THEN immediately compared (_round_count >= rounds_per_match) and _end_match() fires synchronously in the SAME handler that just announced the new round starting -- so with rounds_per_match=3, only rounds 1 and 2 are actually playable; round 3 exists only as a log line. The human wants this cleared (confirmed + a decision recorded) before TK-P2-15 can close, not left as a deferred nit -- this is now gating a real card, not a future TK-P3-04 tuning aside. DECIDE AND FIX ONE OF: (a) semantic fix -- keep rounds_per_match meaning 'N full rounds actually played', i.e. only call _end_match() the NEXT time a Tiger is assigned AFTER the Nth round's own timeout/tag conclusion (effectively check the threshold BEFORE incrementing into a new round, or track 'previous round just concluded' rather than 'a new Tiger was just assigned') -- OR (b) documentation fix -- keep the current trigger-at-assignment behavior exactly as is (it's internally consistent, just means 'assignments before end' not 'rounds played'), but rename/re-document rounds_per_match (var doc + Game_Balance.md/TK-P3-04 handoff note) so the OFF-BY-ONE is explicit and intentional rather than a silent surprise, and confirm the human/designer is fine with a placeholder=3 match actually running 2 played rounds. Given this card exists specifically because the human found the CURRENT behavior confusing/bug-shaped, (a) is very likely the right call unless there's a reason to prefer (b) -- use judgement, but do not silently pick (b) without flagging the tradeoff same as TK-P2-15's own change-control discipline requires (CLAUDE.md: balance changes recorded in 03_Change_Log.md). DoD: re-run CASE E with the fix -- if (a), a rounds_per_match=3 session must show 3 full Tiger reigns each getting real play time before MATCH_END; log/test coverage updated to match whichever semantics is chosen. Blocks TK-P2-15 closure (see that card).
fix_result: FIXED via option (a), the semantic fix (gameplay-engineer, 2026-07-26) -- picked per the note's own steer ('very likely the right call'), justified here rather than silently applied: rounds_per_match now genuinely means N full rounds played, not N Tiger-assignments-before-end, because that is what a real playtester reads the number to mean, and the alternative (b) would have left a placeholder=3 match still only playing 2 rounds by design, i.e. document-the-surprise rather than remove it -- not a good placeholder to hand to TK-P3-03's first real playtest session. Not escalated to designer as a balance-VALUE change (rounds_per_match's placeholder=3 itself is untouched) -- this is a bug fix to what the existing value already means, the same category of fix TK-P2-32/TK-BUG-P2-01 were (wiring/semantics correctness, not a new design decision); flagging here for change-control visibility per CLAUDE.md, no Game_Balance.md/03_Change_Log.md entry made since no design-owned VALUE changed, only a defect in what the code already claimed to do. MECHANISM: the round-end DECISION moved OFF the reactive _on_any_player_role_changed_for_match_end() watcher (which is now a PURE OBSERVER again -- only increments _round_count, decides nothing) and ONTO a new PRE-round-start gate, GameManager.try_reserve_next_round(), which GameManager._run_sequence() (right before the role-swap RPC, AFTER the throw/transform stub animations play -- so the tag that concludes the final round still gets its full step1-3 feedback) and RoundManager._on_round_timeout() (see TK-BUG-P3-02's fix_result for that coupling) must now both call BEFORE performing a swap that would create a new round. When the cap has already been reached (_round_count >= rounds_per_match) while still PLAYING, try_reserve_next_round() refuses the swap AND triggers _end_match() right there instead of ever letting the (rounds_per_match+1)th round start -- so every one of the rounds_per_match rounds that DID start (1..rounds_per_match, each via the counter's own real increment) gets to fully play out to ITS OWN natural conclusion (a tag or a timeout) before the match ends; no phantom round, no zero-play-time final round. This unifies with TK-BUG-P3-02's fix -- 'is a new round currently allowed to start' is the ONE question both bugs needed answered at the SAME checkpoint, see that card's own fix_result. VERIFIED LIVE (end-to-end, not just unit-level) by tests/test_match_end_flow.gd's test_run_sequence_refuses_the_swap_and_ends_the_match_when_the_round_cap_is_reached: with rounds_per_match=2, round 1's concluding tag produces a REAL swap into round 2 (assert match_state stays PLAYING -- the exact assertion that would have failed red against the pre-fix code, since the old code would have ended the match the instant round 2 STARTED), and only round 2's OWN concluding tag (which would create round 3, over the cap) is refused + ends the match. Also tests/test_match_end_flow.gd's RoundManager-side tests confirm the identical semantics for a timeout-driven conclusion. Full regression: GUT 402/402, all 5 non-bot net probes PASS (see TK-BUG-P3-01/02 fix_result for the same numbers, landed together in one run). DoD's own CASE E live re-run (rounds_per_match=3 showing 3 full played reigns) NOT yet performed by me -- did not run tests/net/run_bot_outer.sh per the explicit instruction (TK-P3-09, different agent); stays open pending that human/harness re-run. Files: managers/GameManager.gd (_on_any_player_role_changed_for_match_end() simplified to pure counter, new try_reserve_next_round()/_end_match() idempotency guard, _run_sequence()'s new gate).

THE GAP: managers/GameManager.gd's Tag Sequence holds _is_tag_sequence_active for its full ~1.2s stub duration (step2 throw_stub_sec 0.6s + step3 transform_stub_sec 0.6s of awaits) before the role swap resolves, and TagAbility.host_validate()'s is_sequence_active() gate correctly blocks a SECOND Tag during that window. BUT managers/RoundManager.gd's own timer path is unaware of that lock: _physics_process() keeps accumulating _elapsed_sec while match_state==PLAYING (correct for TK-BUG-P3-02's own purpose), and _on_round_timeout() gates ONLY on GameManager.try_reserve_next_round() (match PLAYING + under the round cap) -- it never consults GameManager.is_sequence_active(). So if the round timer crosses round_duration_sec DURING an in-flight Tag Sequence's stub window, RoundManager broadcasts start_new_round() (a real Tiger re-pick + role swap) while the Tag Sequence is still mid-flight; when that sequence's own _run_sequence() then resumes past its awaits it performs ITS swap too (or, if the timeout's swap already pushed _round_count to the cap, gets refused by try_reserve_next_round()) -- either way an extra, unintended Tiger swap and a _round_count jump for effectively one round's worth of play. SEVERITY = S2 (gameplay), NOT S1: both start_new_round() and apply_role_switch() are @rpc("authority","call_local","reliable") host-authoritative broadcasts, applied in the same order on every peer, so all machines deterministically converge on the SAME final state -- there is no cross-machine desync (no persistent เสือซ้อน/หาย) and no crash. Probability in normal play is low (round_duration_sec is minutes vs a ~1.2s window, ~0.5%/round) so priority=Low, but it is readily reachable in shortened-duration harness/test sessions -- hence a tracked card rather than silently dropped. NOTE: the TK-BUG-P3-02/03 cap gate actually SHRINKS the damage near a match's natural end (a spurious timeout swap at/over the cap is now refused + ends the match cleanly). FIX DIRECTION (confirm by reading, do not assume): the natural fix is to have RoundManager yield a timeout to an in-flight Tag Sequence -- e.g. skip/defer in _on_round_timeout() (or stop accumulating in _physics_process(), or fold it into the shared gate) while GameManager.is_sequence_active() is true, since a Tag Sequence in flight IS a round conclusion already in progress. Read managers/RoundManager.gd's own class doc (the deliberate-minimal-read-only-coupling rationale it already records for TK-BUG-P3-02/03) and GameManager.is_sequence_active() before adding a third read accessor; decide deliberately WHERE the check belongs. DoD: a regression test (Test_Strategy.md section 8 positive-effect assertion) that drives a round timeout while _is_tag_sequence_active is true and asserts no double start_new_round()/apply_role_switch() fires and _round_count advances by exactly one; plus a CASE E harness session (short round_duration_sec) showing no spurious mid-sequence round restart.

title: networking/PlayerSpawner.gd: TEST-MODE-ONLY opt-in so a dedicated host does not spawn its own Player -- prevents the headless bot harness's idle host body from ever being picked/tagged as Tiger and softlocking a match

fix_result: DONE, status -> review (network-engineer, 2026-07-26). Implemented option 1 (true dedicated host, never spawns its own Player) as the human preferred -- a permanent whole-class fix, not the AI-fallback (option 2). HOME OF THE FLAG = NetworkManager autoload (new `dedicated_host_no_self_spawn: bool = false`), NOT scene-local PlayerSpawner -- decided and documented on the var itself (same 'record the autoload-vs-scene-local choice' discipline as TK-P2-15), for two concrete reasons: (1) TK-P3-11's harness sets this at HOST time, right after host() succeeds and BEFORE entering the Waiting Room, when NO PlayerSpawner node exists yet (it lives inside world/TestArena.tscn, unloaded until Start Match) -- a scene-local property literally cannot be set at that moment; (2) PlayerSpawner is recreated FRESH on every TestArena entry (TK-P3-09's WaitingRoom->Arena->WaitingRoom->2nd-Arena re-arm), so a scene-local flag would be lost each scene switch with no natural harness hook to re-apply it, whereas the autoload survives that boundary and every fresh PlayerSpawner reads it. MECHANISM: the decision is a pure static predicate DedicatedHostRules.host_spawns_own_player(is_server, flag) = not (is_server and flag) -- new networking/DedicatedHostRules.gd, same 'pure static helper + thin host-only shell' split as networking/ArenaBarrierRules.gd. PlayerSpawner._do_initial_barrier_spawn() now gates its SOLE host self-spawn (`_spawn_player(multiplayer.get_unique_id())`, line ~347) behind that predicate; every OTHER peer below still spawns in the same order and the barrier/grace-timer machinery is 100% untouched. Confirmed by reading that this is the ONLY host-own-id spawn site in the file: the offline/no-peers immediate path funnels through _do_initial_barrier_spawn() too, and _on_peer_connected()/_rpc_arena_ready() only ever spawn OTHER peers' ids (grep of get_unique_id() in networking/ confirms line 347 is the only spawn use). ZERO changes needed in managers/GameManager.gd or characters/managers/TigerSelector.gd (confirmed by reading, not assuming): GameManager._current_player_ids() builds the first-Tiger candidate pool purely from `_players_root.get_children()` (Players/<id> names) and TigerSelector.pick_first_tiger() only picks from that passed array; Tag/Kick targets resolve via _players_root.get_node_or_null(str(id)). So once the host's Player simply never exists under Players/, the host is automatically unselectable as first Tiger, never a valid apply_role_switch/tag/kick target -- untouched shipped selection logic, exactly as the note required. STRICT NO-OP for the shipped game: flag defaults false, nothing in the shipped build ever sets it, a real human clicking Host always gets their own Player (host_spawns_own_player(true,false)==true). VERIFICATION: (a) new GUT tests/test_dedicated_host_rules.gd (5 assertions, exhaustive 2x2 truth-table: exactly the one (server AND flag) combo skips; client/flag-off/real-host all still spawn) -- node-independent per Test_Strategy.md. (b) full GUT regression GREEN 407/407 (27 scripts, 1832 asserts; was 402/26 before -- +5 tests/+1 script, my additions only, zero pre-existing regressions). (c) all 5 non-bot net probes PASS (run_net_smoke, run_spawn_probe, run_spawn_probe_together, run_tag_detect_probe, run_spawn_probe_slowjoin) -- the together+slowjoin probes exercise the exact barrier/grace machinery this sits next to and prove the flag-OFF real-game path is unregressed. (d) POSITIVE-EFFECT end-to-end check of the flag-ON path via a throwaway 2-instance headless probe (deleted after; NOT committed): host set dedicated_host_no_self_spawn=true, one client joined, both entered TestArena -- after barrier release host asserted Players/ children == [client_id] only, host own id (1) ABSENT, client spawned normally, log showed '[SPAWN] dedicated host (TK-P3-10 no-self-spawn) -- host's own Player intentionally NOT spawned', zero errors -> DEDICATED_HOST_PASS. Godot 4.7.stable headless (C:/Tools/Godot). FILES: networking/NetworkManager.gd (new flag var + doc), networking/PlayerSpawner.gd (guarded self-spawn + _do_initial_barrier_spawn() doc), networking/DedicatedHostRules.gd (new pure helper), tests/test_dedicated_host_rules.gd (new). Did NOT touch tests/net/bot_outer_peer.gd (harness-side wiring is TK-P3-11, tools-devops). Per CLAUDE.md this touches live spawn/authority code in shipped-build files, so BOTH code-reviewer AND qa-engineer must clear it (no dev-tooling exception, even though the feature is test-only); left at review, not flipped to done.

note:
Filed by the human (2026-07-26), a followup gap found continuing from TK-P3-08's own fix while running CASE E again with the re-armed harness (TK-P3-09): TK-P3-07's bot-outer harness has always run its `--role=host` process as what its own doc calls a 'dedicated host' -- but that was only ever true in SPIRIT, not in enforced behavior. networking/PlayerSpawner.gd's readiness-barrier spawn (`_do_initial_barrier_spawn()`) unconditionally spawns a Player for `multiplayer.get_unique_id()` (the host) first, every session, with no opt-out -- so the host harness's own idle body (the human observed target=1, the host's own peer id, being tagged INTO Tiger during a live CASE E run) is a real, selectable, taggable Player like any other. TK-P3-08 already gave the AI to BOTS becoming Tiger; the host process's OWN Player still has none (by design -- TK-P3-07's class doc explicitly frames it as 'own Player stays idle at spawn', a dedicated-server body, not a bot). When host's idle body gets randomly first-picked OR tagged into Tiger, nobody can progress the match (it just stands there) -- softlock until RoundManager's own round_duration_sec timeout (240s placeholder), stalling CASE E testing exactly like TK-P3-08's original bot-idle bug did. The human evaluated two fixes and prefers this one (option 1 of their own writeup): make the host a REAL dedicated host that never spawns a Player for itself at all -- it never enters the arena roster, can never be randomly picked as first Tiger (TigerSelector/GameManager only ever choose among `_players_root`'s actual children), and can never be tagged (there is no Player node under its id to target) -- a permanent, whole-class fix rather than giving yet another idle-body a wander AI (that was the human's own explicitly-NOT-preferred option 2, tracked only as a fallback if this card turns out infeasible).

SCOPE (network-engineer territory -- this is a MultiplayerSpawner/spawn-authority change, per CLAUDE.md's agent roster; do NOT let it leak into managers/GameManager.gd or characters/TigerSelector.gd's own selection logic, matching the exact caution TK-P3-08's own note already laid down for a similar ask: 'any override MUST be strictly confined to the test harness's own code path... ideally with ZERO changes to... the actual selection logic in the shipped build'): add a single new opt-in, default-OFF, TEST-HARNESS-ONLY flag networking/PlayerSpawner.gd (or NetworkManager, whichever is the more natural persistent home -- NetworkManager is an autoload and already survives the WaitingRoom<->Arena boundary, so it can hold this across scene switches without PlayerSpawner needing to re-learn it every fresh TestArena instance; decide and document the choice, same 'record why' discipline TK-P2-15's own autoload-vs-scene-local ruling used) -- e.g. `dedicated_host_no_self_spawn: bool = false`. When true AND `multiplayer.is_server()`, `_do_initial_barrier_spawn()` (and the offline/no-peers `_ready()` immediate-self-spawn branch, and `_on_peer_connected()`'s barrier-window handling) must skip spawning a Player for the host's own id while spawning every OTHER (bot/human) peer completely normally -- the barrier/grace-timer machinery for OTHER peers is untouched. MUST default to false / be a no-op for every real shipped-game session (a real human host always wants their own Player) -- this is a test-tool-only knob, never something a real player's Host button sets. DoD: with the flag enabled, a headless host process never appears in `_players_root`'s children, is never selectable by TigerSelector, is never a valid Tag/Kick target, and every OTHER connected peer (bots, and a real human client if one joins) spawns and plays completely normally including a full MATCH_END->WaitingRoom->2nd-match cycle (TK-P3-09's re-arm). Add regression coverage (GUT, node-independent where possible; a scene-tree test for the barrier-skip-host-only behavior per Test_Strategy.md section 8 if the pure logic alone can't prove it). Mandatory code-reviewer + qa-engineer (touches live spawn/authority code, no CLAUDE.md exception applies even though the FEATURE is test-only -- the CODE lives in shipped-build files). Unblocks TK-P3-11 (harness-side wiring) and, transitively, a clean CASE E re-run.

NetworkManager.dedicated_host_no_self_spawn defaults false; a full-repo grep shows the flag is READ in exactly one place (PlayerSpawner.gd:367) and SET nowhere in shipped code (only TK-P3-11's not-yet-started harness will set it). host_spawns_own_player(true,false)==true, so a human clicking Host is byte-for-byte unaffected.
2) EVERY host-self-spawn site gated: CONFIRMED by reading _ready(), _do_initial_barrier_spawn(), _on_peer_connected(), _rpc_arena_ready(), _on_ready_grace_timeout() in full. The only _spawn_player() call using the host's own id is line 368 inside _do_initial_barrier_spawn(), now gated. Both boot paths funnel through it: offline/no-peers via _ready():288, and the barrier-release/grace via lines 317/459/517. All other _spawn_player() calls (rpc_arena_ready:314 sender_id, peer loop:378, on_peer_connected:487) take a REMOTE peer id -- and get_connected_peer_ids() excludes self (NetworkManager doc L189), so the host's own id can never enter _expected_ready_peers and be spawned via the peer loop. GameManager._current_player_ids() (L607-616) builds the pool purely from _players_root.get_children() name.to_int(); TigerSelector.pick_first_tiger() only picks from that passed array; _pick_first_tiger_with_reroll() re-guards with _players_root.has_node(); tag/kick + apply_role_switch targets resolve via _players_root.get_node_or_null(str(id)) (GameManager L1046/1075/1086/1186, RoundManager L328/334). A never-spawned host has no node under _players_root, so it is automatically unselectable and untaggable -- no selection-logic edits needed.
4) FLAG-HOME (autoload vs scene-local): reasoning HOLDS. PlayerSpawner lives inside TestArena.tscn (unloaded until Start Match) and is recreated fresh each arena entry per TK-P3-09's re-arm; the harness must set the flag at host() time before any spawner node exists. The NetworkManager autoload survives the WaitingRoom<->Arena boundary and is read at barrier time. No simpler/safer alternative missed -- the spawner is scene-constructed so it cannot receive the value any earlier by other means. Matches the ArenaBarrierRules 'pure static helper + host-only shell' split.
5) TEST + REGRESSION: VERIFIED BY RUNNING (Godot 4.7.stable headless, C:/Tools/Godot). tests/test_dedicated_host_rules.gd = 5/5 pass; exhaustive 2x2 truth-table correctly asserts exactly the (server AND flag) combo skips. Ran run_spawn_probe_together.sh (the barrier/grace probe this change sits next to) with the flag OFF: SPAWN TOGETHER: PASS, host+client both spawn, no stack/origin, no pending-spawn error -- flag-OFF real-game path unregressed. (Did not re-run the other 4 net probes; the together-probe is the one that directly exercises the adjacent machinery.)
SCOPE/AUTHORITY: change is confined to network-engineer territory (networking/ + its test); no leak into managers/GameManager.gd or TigerSelector.gd, as the card required. No architecture change (pure additive opt-in following an existing helper pattern); server-authority intact -- the flag is host-local, never replicated, and only decides whether the host spawns its OWN body. Left at status=review; routing to qa-engineer per mandatory dual review (live spawn/authority code).
NON-BLOCKING NITS (do not block approval): (a) Flag ON with NO other peers connected yields an empty arena and GameManager's first-tiger watcher would wait out its grace with 0 players -- already documented in the handoff as an expected test-only misuse (the real harness always has bot peers); worth a QA note only. (b) When the host self-spawn is skipped, _spawn_count is not advanced, so peers start at slot 0 instead of slot 1 -- harmless (SpawnPointUtil wraps, slot identity carries no game meaning) and already called out in the code doc.

INDEPENDENT SAFETY TRACE (not a re-read of code-reviewer): 1) FLAG READ-ONCE / SET-NOWHERE: CONFIRMED by my own grep. NetworkManager.dedicated_host_no_self_spawn (NetworkManager.gd:74, default false) is READ in exactly one place (PlayerSpawner.gd:367) and ASSIGNED nowhere in any .gd file -- the only `dedicated_host_no_self_spawn =` hit in the whole repo is inside _backlog.json prose. The flag lives on the NetworkManager AUTOLOAD (survives scene switches) and is mutated by NO code path; _initial_spawn_done/_spawn_count are per-PlayerSpawner-instance vars recreated fresh each TestArena entry, so every fresh spawner re-reads the same autoload flag at barrier time. No reset/leak path exists -> the flag applies identically every cycle; a 'host-has-Player-in-match-2-but-not-match-1' inconsistency is impossible without external mid-session mutation, which no code performs. 3) NITS -- my own judgement: (a) NON-BLOCKING, but I EXTEND the reviewer's note with the deeper mechanism I found: GameManager._expected_first_tiger_roster_size = 1 + connected_peers (GameManager.gd:491) COUNTS the host. With the flag ON the host never spawns, so the 'have_everyone' fast-path (GM:493/549) is NEVER satisfied EVEN WITH bot peers present -- first-Tiger start always falls through to the FIRST_TIGER_SPAWN_WAIT_GRACE_SEC (12.0s) grace path (GM:560/550), then starts Countdown among the spawned bots. The match still starts and runs correctly (the grace timer is doing exactly its designed rescue job for a never-arriving expected id), and leaving GameManager untouched is the CORRECT call given the card's explicit 'zero changes to selection logic' scope. ACTION ITEM for TK-P3-11 (NOT a blocker here): the harness per-match start-timeout budget MUST exceed ~12s + countdown, because match start is grace-gated (not roster-gated) under this flag. Flag ON with zero other peers = empty arena that idles (GM:564 logs an error, no crash) -- test-only misuse, as documented. (b) _spawn_count not advancing on host-skip: genuinely harmless -- SpawnPointUtil.spawn_point() wraps index % 8 and slot identity carries no game meaning (verified by reading SpawnPointUtil.gd). Non-blocking confirmed. 4) NO INTERACTION with TK-BUG-P3-01 (review-pending-human): CONFIRMED by reading both diffs. That fix lives entirely in GameManager.return_to_waiting_room()/_switch_to_waiting_room() + ui/WaitingRoom.gd and branches on is_server(), which the flag never touches. Arena->WaitingRoom despawn is automatic PlayerSpawner scene-teardown (no explicit host-id despawn call in return_to_waiting_room). A dedicated host simply has one fewer body to despawn -- and its own body was never spawned/replicated to clients -- so the flag can only REDUCE despawn work, never add a race. No shared assumption disturbed. NO S0/S1. No blocking issue found -- NOT routing back to network-engineer. DONE-GATE JUDGEMENT: I am NOT flipping this to done. The shipped-build footprint is a provably inert no-op (independently verified above) and both mandatory reviewers cleared it, BUT the card's DoD is NOT purely automatable -- it explicitly requires the flag-ON path to be exercised across a full MATCH_END->WaitingRoom->2nd-match RE-ARM cycle, which needs a live host that SETS the flag. NO committed automated test sets it (the implementer's flag-ON proof was a throwaway probe, deleted/not committed, and covered only a single match, not the 2nd-match re-arm clause). That live flag-ON verification is definitionally the job of the dependent harness card TK-P3-11. RECOMMENDATION to producer: the automation gate is SUFFICIENT to close TK-P3-10 on its own merits -- its only live behavior is test-tool-only and can never reach a shipped session, and requiring it to wait on TK-P3-11 would INVERT the dependency (TK-P3-11 is blocked on this one). I recommend producer close TK-P3-10 now and let TK-P3-11's own QA prove the live flag-ON re-arm cycle when the harness wiring lands. Left at status=review pending producer's close decision.
